$comment: Published Ingenuity data the checks of expected.json compare against (besides jpl_hover_test.json, which is the only data the rotor model is fitted to). Every entry names its source; 'kind' says whether a value is quoted from text (published) or read off a figure (digitised). build_model.py reads this file.

flight_one.source: H. F. Grip, 'What we're learning about Ingenuity's flight control and aerodynamic performance', NASA Mars Helicopter blog, 2021 (science.nasa.gov/blog/what-were-learning-about-ingenuitys-flight-control-and-aerodynamic-performance/); flight log of Flight One in the NASA Mars Helicopter flight log (science.nasa.gov/mission/mars-2020-perseverance/ingenuity/flight-log/).
flight_one.wind_m_s: 4-6 from the east/south-east, gusting to 8 (MEDA at 1.5 m)
flight_one.notes: The blog quotes the hover rotor power as 'about 210 W' (electrical, both motors), the measured collectives 'about 0.7-0.8 deg lower than predicted', altitude held 'within about 1 cm', heading 'within 1.5 deg', horizontal position variations 'about 25 cm' and cyclic 'generally below 3 deg'.

battery.source: J. Balaram et al., 'Mars Helicopter Technology Demonstrator', AIAA SciTech 2018, AIAA 2018-0023.
battery.flight_budget: 80 % of the flight at 360 W, 20 % at 510 W

cyclic_torque_steps.source: H. F. Grip et al., 'Flight Dynamics of a Mars Helicopter', 43rd European Rotorcraft Forum, 2017, Fig. 15 (JPL system identification on the lower rotor, 25-ft Space Simulator, CO2 at 0.0175 kg/m^3, 2600 rpm).
cyclic_torque_steps.uncertainty: +-0.03 N m from reading the step heights off the figure; the figure shows the measured hub torque responses to 5 deg steps

camrad_mc2_sweep.source: C. Dull, L. Wagner, L. Young, W. Johnson, 'Hover and Forward Flight Performance Modeling of the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter', VFS Aeromechanics for Advanced Vertical Flight Technical Meeting, 2022, Fig. 4 (CAMRAD II, Mars condition 2: rho 0.017 kg/m^3, 2800 rpm, torque-trimmed coaxial pair).
camrad_mc2_sweep.note: A comprehensive-analysis prediction, not a measurement: an independent model of the same rotor, used as a cross-check of the collective-to-thrust relation.

camrad_forward_flight.source: Dull et al. 2022, Fig. 13 (trimmed fuselage pitch) and Fig. 15 (hover rotor power, CAMRAD II / RotCFD).
camrad_forward_flight.note: Reported in the README but not checked: the example's rotor has no H-force from induced drag, so it trims at a smaller pitch in forward flight.

vehicle.source: JPL, 'Mars Helicopter Ingenuity' press kit / quick facts (2021); Dull et al. 2022 (blade mass).
